questions.q: Per this lesson, what kind of information is most valuable to document about a schema object?
options: The non-obvious "why" behind a decision, not the obvious "what" already visible in the CREATE statement
The exact data type of every column, regardless of how obvious it is
The name of the DBA who created the table
Nothing — schema should never be documented outside of source control commit messages
questions.explain: Column names and types are largely self-documenting; what gets lost over time is the reasoning behind non-obvious decisions.

questions.q: What SQL Server mechanism attaches documentation directly to a table, column, or index?
options: Extended properties, added via sp_addextendedproperty
Transaction log backups
Change Data Capture
The tempdb system database
questions.explain: Extended properties are name/value pairs stored with the object itself, added with sp_addextendedproperty.

questions.q: Why does using the extended property name 'MS_Description' specifically matter?
options: SSMS's Object Explorer natively displays it as the object's Description, making it visible without extra tooling
It is the only extended property name SQL Server allows
It automatically syncs to source control
It disables the object from being queried
questions.explain: MS_Description is the well-known name SSMS recognizes and surfaces directly in the Object Explorer UI.

questions.q: Which example from this lesson illustrates a column worth documenting?
options: A column that looks unused but is still written to by a legacy nightly job, where removing it would break that job
An OrderDate column typed as date
A primary key column named Id
A column whose name matches its business meaning exactly
questions.explain: The lesson's test for what's worth documenting is whether a competent DBA looking at the object cold would have a reasonable question — an unused-looking column that's actually load-bearing clearly qualifies.

questions.q: Where can existing extended properties be queried from?
options: sys.extended_properties
sys.change_tracking_tables
sys.dm_exec_requests
msdb.dbo.sysjobs
questions.explain: sys.extended_properties is the catalog view for reading back extended properties already attached to objects.
